name: 陳雅玫
objective: This course develops students’ human-centered GenAI literacy through the design and adaptation of Custom GPTs and multi-step agent workflows for authentic translation projects on the Global Voices Lingua platform. The course is organized around three progressive project cycles: political and social affairs, science and the environment, and culture and marginalized voices. Across these cycles, students place human-AI collaboration at the center of translation decision-making. Working in groups, students move beyond passive AI use by adapting instructor-scaffolded Custom GPT instructions and configuring visual Dify agent workflow templates for domain-specific translation tasks. They test these adapted tools on authentic Lingua texts, compare AI-generated suggestions with their own translation judgments, and design explicit human review checkpoints to identify where automated assistance must give way to human oversight. Each project cycle follows a Plan–Translate–Reflect structure. This ensures that every modification to a prompt, workflow step, or verification criterion is guided by translation reasoning rather than technical novelty alone. By the end of the course, students will be prepared for contemporary translation practice not only by learning how to use AI tools, but also by learning how to shape, question, and take responsibility for the human-AI workflows that support translation.
